title: Palliative care at home
also: caring for a seriously ill person at home
what: Doctors and nurses come to the home of a seriously ill person. They relieve pain and other symptoms and help the family.
why: For a serious illness that cannot be cured, when the main aim is to reduce pain and make life calmer.
duration: a visit usually takes 30 to 60 minutes, follow-up for as long as needed
tell_doctor: Which symptoms bother the person most: pain, shortness of breath, nausea, sleeplessness
Which medicines the person gets and how they cope with them
Whether they can eat, drink and get up
Who is giving care and what is hard
The person's own wishes about treatment

prepare.title: Referral
prepare.text: A doctor's report on palliative status is usually needed. Ask your clinic how to get it.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Gather all the medicines and notes of when they were given.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Write down what worries you as the caregiver.

steps: The team arrives at the set time
The doctor asks questions and examines the patient
A nurse shows how to give care
You agree on the next visit and how to be in touch
feel: It can be hard for close ones - the team supports the family too
after: Give the medicines exactly by the schedule
Write down how the pain changes
Call the service if things get worse - do not wait for the next visit
red_flags: Severe pain that medicines do not relieve - call the palliative service
Hard breathing, bleeding or seizures - call your local emergency number or the service

faq.q: Is palliative care only for the last days?
faq.a: No. Help can be received for a long time, so that the person feels better.

faq.q: Can I get pain relief at home?
faq.a: Yes, the doctor will choose and prescribe the needed medicines.

reminders.text: Palliative service visit tomorrow. Gather all the medicines and write down what worries you.
